method: Full manual read of every CMS write endpoint's source (not just pattern matching), plus a targeted grep across the merged code for unsafe spread/passthrough patterns.

unsafe_pattern_scan.result: CLEAN — no endpoint spreads arbitrary request-body JSON into establishments.update()

endpoints.who_calls_it: Authenticated establishment owner (via the CMS editor UI)
endpoints.authorization: Establishment re-derived server-side from owner_id = session user id — a client-supplied establishment id is never trusted
endpoints.row_ownership_check: Both at the app layer (.eq('owner_id', context.userId)) AND enforced again by RLS on the session-bound client (not service role)
endpoints.field_whitelist: Explicit Set: phone, email, website, address, city — any other key in the request body causes a 400 rejection before any DB call
endpoints.service_role_usage: NONE — uses the session-bound client throughout
endpoints.registry_field_exposure: NONE — official_id/source_ministry/etc. are not in the whitelist and could not reach establishments.update() even if included in the payload

endpoints.field_whitelist: Explicit Set: description only, length-capped at 4000 chars

endpoints.row_ownership_check: establishment_id is set server-side from context.establishmentId, never from the request body
endpoints.field_whitelist: Fixed set of 8 known section_key values; rejects unknown keys, duplicates, and incomplete sets; writes only to school_page_sections (not establishments at all)
endpoints.registry_field_exposure: N/A — different table entirely, no establishments columns touched

double_defense_note: Even in the hypothetical case where a future code change accidentally widened one of these allowlists to include a registry-protected field, the write would STILL be blocked at the database layer by migration 0023's trigger (re-verified live this sprint, unaffected by this integration) — this is genuine defense-in-depth, not a single point of failure.
if_service_role_endpoint_blindly_trusted: Not found. No CMS endpoint uses the service-role client at all in this branch.
overall: PASS — no CMS endpoint reopens the Registry vulnerability, at either the app layer or the DB layer.
